correctness.rationale: For the specified heavy-over-light inviscid normal mode, unit interface displacement gives upper/lower interface velocity potentials −Γ coth(kh)/k and +Γ coth(k(L−h))/k; the hydrostatic jump and tension give Γ²D=k(G−σk²). At fixed k, the coth addition formula writes D=(a+b)coth S+(at+b/t)/sinh S for S=kL and t=sinh(k(L−h))/sinh(kh). The minimum is unique because t decreases bijectively from infinity to zero and equality in AM–GM fixes t=√(b/a). The allocation formula, strict half/square-root-share bounds, monotonicity in S and equal-depth deficit follow from this equality (z coth z is strictly increasing). The optimized denominator is a positive mixture of coth S and coth(S/2). Each component's negative logarithmic derivative q=2kd/sinh(2kd) strictly decreases; differentiation of the weighted mean gives mean(q′) minus Var(q), with the derivative in log k, so the elasticity drops strictly from 2 to 1. Its crossing with the increasing capillary term gives the unique maximum in scalar k, with k_c/√3<k_*<k_c/√2. At this crossing, increasing L lowers the elasticity at fixed k and shifts the crossing to smaller k, while D_* decreases pointwise and the maximum growth increases. The bounds keep k_* away from zero in the L limits, giving the stated wavenumbers, growth constants and thickness offset from the exact formulas. This is not uniqueness of a horizontal propagation direction. Read the frozen verification notes and script; the reported finite tests are corroboration, not the proof. The decision uses the analytic check, not execution of the supplied script.
